newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek Xiosbank says 96 pretax up 20pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek Xiosbank says 96 pretax up 20pct.

text.p: Greece's private Xiosbank whose IPO prospectus was approved today by the Athens stock exchange said its 1996 pretax profits rose 20 percent to 2.1 billion drachmas and are projected to increase to 2.7 billion in 1997.
The bank will issue 1.592 million new registered shares to the public and 79,610 shares will be privately placed to raise more than 4.0 billion drachmas, it said.
The IPO share price will be determined a few days before public subscription.

The IPO proceeds will be used to finance part of the bank's 1997-2000 investment programme. The programme involves the expansion of its branch network by 20 to 45 branches by 2000 and the modernisation of its technological infrastructure.
The National Bank of Greece will be the lead underwriter and Telesis Capital will serve as the issue advisor.
Lending rose 24 percent to 103 billion drachmas in 1996, the bank said.
The bank has a market share of 9.0 percent in consumer loans and 8.0 percent in auto loans. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
